text:
Sanjay Iyer: Quick sync — we surfaced a regression where enabling continuous batching dropped prefix KV-cache hit-rate on some prod routes from ~82% -> ~58% after the September rollout. Any early theories? :thinking:
Olivia Park: Interesting. Are the requests mixing different prompts/prefixes in the same batches? continuous batching can compose heterogeneous queues which may reduce identical-prefix coalescing.
A.J. Chen: Yep that was my first thought. If batch composition groups by arrival time only, you lose prefix locality. Do we have per-batch prefix-entropy metrics?
Mia Rodriguez: I pulled the perf traces. Short summary: warm routes for chat completions that rely on shared system prompts dropped hit rate. I attached a quick sample from the kv-cache telemetry:
```
# kv-cache telemetry sample (per-minute aggregated)
model: redwood-13b-ops, route: /v1/chat, time: 2025-10-03T12:00
requests: 3200, cache_lookups: 3100, cache_hits: 1800, hit_rate: 0.58
prev_week: hit_rate: 0.82 (continuous-batching disabled)
avg_batch_size: 12.1, pct_batches_mixed_prefix: 68%
```
Olivia Park: That pct_batches_mixed_prefix number is telling. If 2/3 of batches are mixing prefixes, cold KV keys won't be reused in the same forward pass.
Sanjay Iyer: Can kernel selection be affecting this? e.g. different runtimes causing different memory layouts that affect KV lookup performance?
A.J. Chen: Kernel selection impacts per-token latency not the logical cache-keying. The hit-rate change is about whether the same prefix keys are present in the KV cache when a request runs. I doubt kernel choice caused the hit-rate drop.
perf-bot: Regression alert: prefix-cache-hit_rate for model redwood-13b-ops on /v1/chat dropped 29% at 2025-10-02T23:12 UTC.
Mia Rodriguez: I ran a microbench comparing batching strategies locally. Two variants: time-windowed batching (current continuous) vs prefix-aware bucketing. Results (p95 latency / effective hit-rate):
```
continuous-batching: p95=210ms, hit_rate=0.59
prefix-bucketed:     p95=230ms, hit_rate=0.80
```
So prefix bucketing regained hit-rate but increased tail latency slightly.
Olivia Park: That's the classic latency vs cost/throughput trade. Higher hit-rate reduces compute and shortens mean latency but bucketed batching increases queueing for rare prefixes.
Sanjay Iyer: Do we have token-cost impact numbers? Mia, any estimate on tokens saved per 1% hit-rate improvement?
Mia Rodriguez: Roughly: per-request token-work reduces by ~0.9 tokens per 1% hit-rate for these routes (because prefix lengths are ~40 tokens and cache avoids decoding those). So 20% hit-rate gain ~18 tokens saved/request -> significant at scale.
A.J. Chen: Operational options: 1) softer prefix grouping (try to maximize prefix homogeneity without strict bucketing), 2) pre-warm popular prefixes into KV prior to serving burst, 3) hybrid: use prefix-bucketing for top-N prefixes and continuous-batching for long-tail.
Olivia Park: On keying: current key is full prefix string normalized + model+device. Might get collisions or misses if small whitespace differences exist. We should consider canonicalizing (whitespace, normalized tokens) or use tokenized-prefix hash.
Mia Rodriguez: Agreed. I benchmarked two cache-key schemes: raw-string vs tokenized-hash. Tokenized-hash improved dedup by ~3% because it collapsed minor formatting diffs.
Sanjay Iyer: Warmup strategies? What about synthetic warmup requests that populate KV for top prefixes during deploys?
Mia Rodriguez: We tried deploy warmup in staging. Simple approach: after model load, issue N synthetic requests that each contain the most frequent prefixes. Warmup latency added during deploy but steady-state hit-rate improved within minutes. Logs: 
```
2025-10-03T05:00 deploy-start
2025-10-03T05:00 issue-warmup: 120 requests for top-10 prefixes
2025-10-03T05:02 warmup-complete, observed cache_hit_rate: 0.79
```
Olivia Park: Warmup helps for scaleups, but doesn't solve composition effects during mixed incoming traffic.
A.J. Chen: Another idea: adapt batch formation heuristics to prefer siblings with same prefix when queue depth is low. E.g., wait up to X ms to coalesce by prefix if expected throughput low. Add a per-route knob: latency_sensitivity threshold.
Sanjay Iyer: Can we get per-route analytics: histogram of prefix-entropy per batch, hit-rate, p95 latency — so PMs can set policies?
Mia Rodriguez: Currently we emit batch metrics but not prefix-entropy. I'll add instrumentation: per-batch unique-prefix-count, batch-size, hit-rate. Low overhead aggregation.
perf-bot: Note: adding per-batch instrumentation increased metrics throughput, watch prometheus scrape costs.
Sanjay Iyer: Practical mitigations for now?
Olivia Park: Rollback continuous-batching for the most sensitive chat route (flagged) and enable hybrid strategy on canary. Also start tokenized-hash keying experiment.
A.J. Chen: I'll prototype a prefix-aware coalescer with soft-wait (max 8ms) and evaluate p95/throughput tradeoffs.
Mia Rodriguez: I'll run a 48h A/B in prod: control = continuous-batching, variant = hybrid (top-100 prefixes bucketed + warmup + tokenized-key). Collect p95, hit-rate, token-cost/cpu.
Sanjay Iyer: Cool. Action items:
- A.J. implement soft-wait coalescer PR and perf tests (owner: A.J, ETA: 2025-10-10)
- Mia run 48h A/B and produce cost/hit-rate dashboard (owner: Mia, ETA: 2025-10-12)
- Olivia add prefix-entropy per-batch metric and expose per-route (owner: Olivia, ETA: 2025-10-08)
- Ops: rollback continuous-batching on /v1/chat canary if A/B shows regression (owner: deploy-bot)
Sanjay Iyer: Thanks all. Any objections? :thumbsup:
Olivia Park: +1
A.J. Chen: +1
Mia Rodriguez: +1
deploy-bot: scheduled rollback flag created for /v1/chat (canary) if metrics degrade
perf-bot: Will monitor and post alerts to this thread if delta > 10% hit-rate or p95 > 250ms
Sanjay Iyer: I'll follow up with short retro after A/B. Closing thread for now.
